skill.name: git
skill.description: Git workflow management including branch validation, commit conventions, PR preparation, and repository health checks.
skill.summary: Guides Git branch checks, conventional commits, pull request preparation, and repository health reviews.
skill.author: ByronWilliamsCPA

content.value_statement: Teams often lose time checking branch names, commit format, and pull request readiness. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code structured Git workflow guidance.
actual_capabilities: Reviews current branch and repository status commands.
Defines accepted branch prefixes and naming patterns.
Supports pull request preparation and validation checklist workflows.
Maps branch prefixes and commit types to release impact.
Activates on common Git, branch, commit, and pull request terms.
limitations: It is a prompt-only skill and does not execute Git commands by itself.
It assumes Git is installed and the user is inside a repository.
Referenced workflow files are not included in this package.
It does not replace project-specific branch protection or review rules.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Clean Commit
use_cases.description: Generate a conventional commit structure after reviewing changed files and branch context.

use_cases.title: Validate Pull Request Readiness
use_cases.description: Check branch naming, repository status, and pull request checklist items before requesting review.

use_cases.title: Standardize Release Workflows
use_cases.description: Align branch prefixes and commit types with semantic release expectations.

prompt_templates.title: Check My Branch
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my current Git branch name and status. Tell me whether it matches the expected branch format.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Commit Message
prompt_templates.prompt: Use my staged changes to draft a conventional commit message with type, optional scope, description, body, and footer.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Pull Request
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my branch, recent commits, and repository status. Draft a pull request summary and readiness checklist.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Release Impact
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze my branch prefix and commit types. Explain the expected semantic release impact and any workflow risks.

output_examples.input: I am on feat/cart-discounts and need a commit message for staged pricing changes.
output_examples.output: A conventional commit recommendation with type feat, a concise description, optional body notes, and any relevant footer guidance.

output_examples.input: Check whether my fix branch is ready for a pull request.
output_examples.output: A readiness review covering branch naming, repository status, commit quality, and pull request checklist items.

output_examples.input: Explain the release impact of my perf branch and recent commits.
output_examples.output: A release impact summary that maps the branch prefix and commit types to patch, minor, or no-release outcomes.

best_practices: Run repository status checks before drafting commits or pull requests.
Use descriptive branch slugs that match the documented prefix list.
Review release impact before merging feature, fix, performance, or hotfix work.
anti_patterns: Do not create generic commit messages without checking changed files.
Do not ignore branch naming rules when preparing a pull request.
Do not assume release impact without reviewing branch prefix and commit type.

faq.question: Does this skill execute Git commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides workflow guidance and command examples for the AI assistant and user to apply.

faq.question: Which branch prefixes does it document?
faq.answer: It documents feat, fix, docs, refactor, perf, test, chore, and hotfix prefixes.

faq.question: Does it support conventional commits?
faq.answer: Yes. It guides commit messages with type, optional scope, description, body, and footer sections.

faq.question: Can it prepare pull request content?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes workflows for pull request description generation, validation, and checklist review.

faq.question: Does it include project-specific Git rules?
faq.answer: No. It provides general workflow guidance that teams should adapt to their repository rules.

faq.question: Can it help with semantic release planning?
faq.answer: Yes. It maps branch prefixes and commit types to expected version impact.
